federationPackage.note: thehub-pr owns federation-design/, so this is not a version pin — the app always builds against whatever is currently checked in at federation-design/packages/react, resolved via npm's file: symlink (confirmed: node_modules/@pr-federation/react -> ../../federation-design/packages/react).
otherConsumption: server/frontend/src/main.jsx imports '@federation-design/styles/federation.css' directly (design tokens consumed via CSS custom properties / Tailwind, not via JS component imports).

server/frontend/src/lib/theme.jsx is a hand-vendored reimplementation of the package's ThemeProvider/useTheme (its own header comment says so: 'Mirrors the canonical federation ThemeProvider (@pr-federation/react) but is vendored locally so this app builds standalone and offline'). It is NOT FederationThemeProvider/useFederationTheme — no import of either symbol exists anywhere in server/frontend/src.

controlSourceMap.button: local shadcn/ui primitive (src/components/ui/button.jsx) — Radix Slot + class-variance-authority. NOT FederationButton (0 usages found anywhere in src/). Height: default 36px (h-9), sm 32px (h-8), lg 40px (h-10), icon 36px (h-9 w-9) — none of the four size variants reach the 44px CSS-px touch-target minimum the test-harness contract requires.
controlSourceMap.dialog: local shadcn/ui primitive (src/components/ui/dialog.jsx) built on @radix-ui/react-dialog. NOT a Federation* component (the package exports no dialog/modal primitive at all).
controlSourceMap.sheet: local shadcn/ui primitive (src/components/ui/sheet.jsx), also built on @radix-ui/react-dialog (Radix Dialog styled as a slide-in panel). Used for the record-create/edit flows (e.g. Cases 'New Case').
controlSourceMap.toggleSwitch: local shadcn/ui primitive (src/components/ui/switch.jsx) built on @radix-ui/react-switch. NOT a Federation* component. Thumb track is 20x36px (h-5 w-9), well under the 44px touch-target minimum.
controlSourceMap.statusBadge: bespoke JSX, not FederationStatusBadge/FederationSemanticBadge despite both being exported by the package. The general-purpose one is src/components/shared/StatusChip.jsx (renders a value through a per-page color map from src/lib/chips.js) and is reused across ~35 pages/components (Cases, Gates, Sources, Programs, Dashboard, Manifest, Dictionary, Spiderweb, Skywatcher, Centinelas, MoneySweep, AguaYLuz, Ovnis, Operations, RecentActivity, Integrations, and task/crossover/audit/manager/feed subcomponents). A second bespoke variant, src/components/tasks/LinkageBadge.jsx, exists specifically for task linkage state (Linked/Unlinked) but did not render in this pass because the diagnostic-mode seed data had zero Federation Tasks.
controlSourceMap.emptyState: @pr-federation/react FederationEmptyState — the ONLY Federation* component actually consumed in this repo's UI, wrapped by src/components/shared/EmptyState.jsx. That wrapper's own comment states thehub-pr's EmptyState was the reference implementation FederationEmptyState was modeled on, i.e. this repo is both the design system's source-of-truth repo and (for this one control) a genuine consumer of its own published component.
controlSourceMap.loadingState: bespoke JSX — src/components/shared/RouteFallback.jsx (full-screen spinner div, role="status") for route-level loading, plus ad hoc src/components/ui/skeleton.jsx usage (only 1 call site: src/pages/Operations.jsx). NOT FederationLoadingState/FederationAsyncState.
controlSourceMap.errorState: bespoke JSX — src/components/ErrorBoundary.jsx (render-time React error boundary, role="alert"). No dedicated component for data-fetch/API error states was found; pages appear to handle fetch failures ad hoc or fall through to StatusChip/EmptyState. NOT FederationErrorState.

themeSupport.toggleComponent: src/components/shared/ThemeToggle.jsx, rendered in src/components/layout/Sidebar.jsx and src/components/layout/MobileNav.jsx — reachable on every route in both desktop and mobile layouts.
themeSupport.implementation: src/lib/theme.jsx — a local, hand-vendored ThemeProvider/useTheme, explicitly NOT an import of FederationThemeProvider/useFederationTheme from @pr-federation/react (see federationPackage.otherConsumption above). It writes both the Tailwind '.dark' class and the federation.css 'data-theme' attribute so the vendored provider and the canonical CSS tokens stay in agreement despite the JS provider itself not being the canonical one.
